paper.title: Generalized Thompson Sampling for Contextual Bandits

settings.name_in_paper: Contextual bandits with a finite set of experts (realizable)
unmapped: learner uses a (possibly misspecified) prior p over the N experts; bounds depend on p_1, the prior weight of the true expert
the learner knows the loss-related constant kappa_2 used to set eta
settings.definition_quote: Learner observes the context $x_t\in\InputSet$, where $x_t$ can be chosen by an adversary. Learner selects arm $a_t\in\ActionSet$, and receives reward $r_t\in\{0,1\}$, with expectation $\mu(x_t,a_t)$. ... we make the realization assumption that one of the experts, $\expert^*\in\expert$, correctly predicts the average reward.

settings.name_in_paper: Contextual bandits with experts, Bayes regret under unknown true prior p*
unmapped: the optimal expert is drawn from an unknown true prior p*, while the learner uses a possibly different prior p
the learner knows the loss-related constant kappa_2 used to set eta
settings.definition_quote: one can assume the optimal expert, $\expert^*$, is drawn from an \emph{unknown} prior distribution, $\vecb{p}^*$. The expected $T$-step \emph{Bayes regret} can then be defined: $R(T,\vecb{p}^*) \defeq \E_{\expert^*\sim\vecb{p}^*}\left[R(T)\right]$.

symbols.L_bar: expected total average shifted loss E[sum_t bar l_t]
symbols.gamma_mix: uniform-exploration mixing parameter gamma of the algorithm

conditions: Condition C2 (informativeness): Delta_i(x_t) <= kappa_1 sqrt(bar l_t)
realizability: one expert predicts mu exactly

source.label: thm:main
source.quote: Under Conditions~\cref{cond:consistency} and \cref{cond:informativeness}, the expected $T$-step regret of Generalized Thompson Sampling is \[ R(T) \le \kappa_1\sqrt{T\cdot\E\left[\sum_{t=1}^T\bar{l}_t\right]} + \gamma T . \]

results.notes: Generic reduction bound depending on the expected total shifted loss. Regret defined via means against best expert, hence pseudo_regret.

symbols.p_1: prior weight assigned by the learner to the true expert

source.label: lem:lbar
source.quote: Under Conditions~\cref{cond:boundedness} and \cref{cond:selfboundedness}, with $\eta$ chosen to be $(2(e-2)\kappa_2)^{-1}$, the expected total shifted loss of \gts\ is bounded by a constant independent of $T$: \[ \sum_{t=1}^T\bar{l}_t \le 4(e-2)\kappa_2\ln\frac{1}{p_1} . \]

results.notes: Bound on expected total shifted (prediction) loss, not regret.

symbols.p_1: prior weight of the true expert

source.label: cor:main
source.quote: Under the conditions of \thmref{thm:main} and \lemref{lem:lbar}, the expected $T$-step regret of \gts is at most \[ \sqrt{4\kappa_2(e-2)}\kappa_1(1-\gamma)\sqrt{T\cdot\ln\frac{1}{p_1}} + \gamma T . \]

results.notes: kappa_1 may depend on gamma (e.g. sqrt(2K/gamma) for square loss).

symbols.H_pstar: entropy of the true prior p*
symbols.KL_prior: KL divergence d_KL(p*, p) between true prior and learner's prior

conditions: optimal expert drawn from unknown prior p*

source.label: cor:average
source.quote: If the optimal expert is sampled from distribution $\vecb{p}^*$, the Bayes regret is at most \[ R(T,\vecb{p}^*) \le \sqrt{4\kappa_2(e-2)}\kappa_1(1-\gamma)\sqrt{T\left(H(\vecb{p}^*)+\kld{\vecb{p}^*}{\vecb{p}}\right)} + \gamma T ,\]

results.notes: Bayes regret w.r.t. the true (unknown) prior p*, not the learner's prior.

symbols.p_1: prior weight of the true expert

conditions: square loss used for weight updates

source.label: sec:squareloss
source.quote: Plugging these values in \corref{cor:main} and choosing $\gamma=\Theta\left(\sqrt[3]{K/T}\right)$, we obtain the regret bound of $O\left(\sqrt{\ln\frac{1}{p_1}}K^{1/3}T^{2/3}\right)$

results.notes: Stated in text, not a numbered theorem; uses kappa_1 = sqrt(2K/gamma), kappa_2 = 4 from Agarwal et al. 2012. Bayes version O(sqrt(H(p*)+KL) K^{1/3} T^{2/3}) also stated.

symbols.beta_log: bound such that shifted logarithmic losses lie in [-beta/2, beta/2]
symbols.p_1: prior weight of the true expert

conditions: logarithmic loss used for weight updates
shifted log losses of all experts bounded in [-beta/2, beta/2]
tuning: gamma tuned as a function of K, T (not explicit)

source.label: sec:logloss
source.quote: With all four conditions verified, we can apply results in \secref{sec:main} to reach the regret bound of $O\left(K^{\frac{2}{3}}\beta^{\frac{1}{3}}T^{\frac{2}{3}}\sqrt{\ln\frac{1}{p_1}}\right)$

results.notes: Stated in text; relies on Lemma 3 whose proof is only sketched. Bayes version O(K^{2/3} beta^{1/3} T^{2/3} sqrt(H(w*)+KL(w*,w))) also stated. Covers Thompson Sampling as special case (log loss).
